Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a recipe into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Country Loaf: Two Boules, One Dutch Oven for one batch, two 900 g boules
Resource limits: one oven, one dutch oven, one refrigerator, one baker, the two loaves bake one after the other.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Country Loaf: Two Boules, One Dutch Oven

One batch of dough, two loaves, and a single dutch oven that has to bake them one after the other. One oven, one baker, one refrigerator. Times count from eight in the morning; the loaves come out of the fridge the next day.

Levain
Mix 50 g of ripe starter with 100 g of flour and 100 g of water in a jar; 5 minutes. Leave the jar at room temperature until it domes and smells sweet, 4 to 6 hours.

Dough
Weigh the flour, water and salt for the whole bake first thing; 10 minutes. At half past eight, whisk 900 g of flour into 680 g of water; 5 minutes. Let it autolyse for 1 hour. When the levain is ripe, squeeze it into the autolysed dough with 20 g of salt and work it by hand for 10 minutes. Bulk ferment at 24°C until the dough has risen by half, 3 to 5 hours. Fold the dough in the bowl half an hour after mixing, again half an hour later, and a third time after another half hour; each fold takes 2 minutes.

Divide and shape
Tip the dough out, cut it in two and preshape each piece into a loose round; 10 minutes. Let the rounds rest on the bench for 25 minutes. Shape both boules tightly and settle them into floured bannetons; 10 minutes. Retard them in the refrigerator, 10 to 14 hours.

Bake
Three quarters of an hour before the dough comes out, put the dutch oven in the oven and heat both to 250°C. Score the first loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the first loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it and bake for another 20 minutes until the crust is dark. Cool it on a rack for at least an hour before cutting. Re-heat the empty dutch oven for 10 minutes. Score the second loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the second loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it for a final 20 minutes. Cool the second loaf on the rack beside the first.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

Reading the full text: this is a one-batch, two-loaf (two 900 g boules) sourdough country bread bake, run by a single baker with a single oven, a single dutch oven, and a single refrigerator, so it's one long single-actor process rather than a multi-person kitchen. It starts from a levain build (starter + flour + water, mixed then left 4–6 hours to ripen) that must be ready before it's folded into the main dough; the dough itself is mixed in stages (flour/water autolyse for an hour, then levain and salt worked in), bulk-fermented 3–5 hours with three timed folds at 30-minute intervals early in bulk, then divided, preshaped, bench-rested, shaped into two bannetons, and retarded in the fridge overnight (10–14 hours, explicitly finishing "the next day"). Baking requires preheating the oven and the single dutch oven for 45 minutes, then baking the two boules one after another in that one dutch oven — score/load, 20 minutes covered, 20 minutes uncovered, then a 10-minute reheat of the empty dutch oven before repeating for the second loaf — with each loaf cooling on a rack for at least an hour before cutting. No explicit finish deadline is given, so the schedule should just run start-to-finish as early as the equipment and rest/ferment times allow, respecting that only one loaf can occupy the dutch oven at a time, only one baker is doing all the hands-on work, and the fridge holds both shaped loaves through the long overnight retard. Nothing appears truncated — the source text reads as a complete recipe from levain through both loaves cooling.

  "servesOrScale": "1 batch, 2 boules of 900 g each",
  "deadline": "none given — finish as early as the work allows",

A track is a single line of sequential work — one thing happening after another with no gaps — and here I'll need separate tracks for the levain (which sits and ripens on its own timeline), the dough (mix, autolyse, fold, bulk, divide/shape, retard), and the bake (preheat, load/bake/cool for each loaf), since these run in parallel or interleave rather than strictly one after another. Each step carries exactly one duration kind: most of this recipe is `fixed` (mixing, folding, baking segments, cooling), but the levain ripening, bulk fermentation, and cold retard are given as ranges ("4 to 6 hours", "3 to 5 hours", "10 to 14 hours") so those should be `variable` with min/max/default. StartTriggers wire the tracks together — the dough's fold-in-levain step must wait on the levain track via `afterStep`, and the bake track's first load waits on the dough track's retard step — while `programStart` anchors the very first steps and `programStartOffset` can delay a track if needed, though here everything cascades naturally from prior steps. All `stepId`s must be unique across the whole program even though steps live in different tracks. Every task a step claims — the oven, the dutch oven, the refrigerator, the baker's own two hands, the cooling rack — needs a `resourceConstraints` entry whose `maxConcurrent` enforces the real bottleneck, most obviously the single dutch oven that forces the two loaves' bakes to be sequential. Since the two boules bake one after another with the same shape of step (score/load, covered bake, uncovered bake, cool), that's a natural `replicates: {count: 2, mode: "serial"}` on the bake step rather than duplicated steps, with the reheat and cooling chained per instance and the cooling rack sized to hold both loaves at once.

Resource constraints expected:
- baker: maxConcurrent 1 (the one person doing all hands-on mixing, folding, shaping, scoring, loading — these can't overlap)
- oven: maxConcurrent 1 (the single oven housing the dutch oven)
- dutchOven: maxConcurrent 1 (forces the two bakes to be sequential, one loaf at a time)
- fridge: maxConcurrent 1 (both shaped boules retard together in a single overnight session)
- rack: maxConcurrent 2 (both loaves can cool side by side once baked)

Actors: 1 (a single baker performs every hands-on step; nothing here is done by a second person).

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else.
